title: Choose the visual world
question: Choose the visual world for the clarity-from-chaos reset.

options.label: Clarity Workbench
options.lineage: student annotation desks, index systems, and marked-up working notes
options.thesis: The study kit is a work surface: messy source enters at the left, the next useful move is marked at the right.
options.viewport: A left-aligned promise meets a live clarity board: source fragments, a guide outline, one flashcard, and a practice prompt connected by a single signal rail.
options.risk: Reads like stationery if the transformation remains decorative instead of showing the next study action.

raised.raise: The grid is a functional alignment armature shared by source fragments, guide sections, and answer states, not background decoration.
Progress is a persistent mark on a sequence, so completed, current, and deferred study work never vanish.
Flat planes and quiet negative space make the one signal action legible before ornament enters.

options.label: Cell-built Study Sheet
options.thesis: Understanding is assembled cell by cell, and the visible grid proves how dense notes become a navigable kit.
options.viewport: A large cell-built statement anchors the source-to-kit sequence; selecting a cell reveals the learning unit it supports.
options.case: Strong product clarity and a credible study grammar; it holds one axis but is less immediately student-identifying than a workbench.
options.risk: Becomes a typographic exercise if the grid does not map to real study units.
options.kept: Keep the functional grid as the shared alignment system.

options.label: Study Edit Rail
options.lineage: film cutting benches and punched work prints
options.thesis: A study session is an editable sequence: source, guide, recall, and test stay reachable on one rail.
options.viewport: The first view is a horizontal study sequence with the current step flagged and deferred material hanging below for return.
options.case: Excellent state vocabulary and strong clarity for the workspace; it holds one axis but can feel too tool-like for a first-time student landing.
options.risk: Scrubbing and rail metaphors could make a simple study action feel like editing software.
options.kept: Keep state as a mark, not a hue, across generation and review states.

options.label: Plane-by-Plane Recall
options.thesis: A topic becomes recognizable when only the essential planes remain.
options.viewport: A few responsive planes compose the learning path, with each plane naming the role it plays.
options.case: Clear visual restraint, but the metaphor does not explain the student's source-to-study workflow quickly enough.
options.risk: Can reduce real study content to an abstract poster.
options.kept: Keep its discipline of flat, non-competing planes in the workbench's clarity board.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional centered SaaS hero with a screenshot, feature cards, and a single signup button.
canonCard.viewport: The expected marketing arrangement, executed cleanly.
canonCard.risk: The product becomes interchangeable and the clarity mechanism stays implicit.
